rows.title: The Intervention Knowledge Bottleneck: Convergent Failure at Entity-Level Modification Knowledge
rows.required_unit: A third independent self-evolution mechanism with first-party, source-native units that directly measure the same entity-level modification/intervention-knowledge endpoint as the frozen candidate, with at least 8 aligned units across at least 3 mutation/operation types, plus a source-native comparison showing that the failure persists under more single-turn or non-entity-grounded data and changes under targeted entity-grounded or multi-turn intervention evidence.
rows.asset_audit: Canonical source audit found a more basic comparability gap before third-method execution: SkillForge directly measures project-specific/entity-level intervention-knowledge ablation, whereas SkillEvo directly measures single-turn feedback-gradient saturation versus multi-turn feedback and does not directly label that endpoint as entity-level modification knowledge. Reviewed first-party near-neighbors (MindMemOS, EvoGraph-R1, SciToolAgent-Evo, EvoSOP, DeepSearch-Evolve, Agentic ESOpt, AI4AI-Bench) either measure a different entity/schema/tool/algorithm object, lack the frozen operation headroom, or are benchmarks rather than an independent acquisition mechanism. No >=8-unit / >=3-operation source-native third-mechanism table for the frozen endpoint is currently available.
rows.reopen_only_if: Reopen only after primary or author-released first-party evidence closes both missing conditions: (1) SkillEvo or a reformulated independent source directly exposes a source-defined entity-level modification/intervention-knowledge endpoint comparable to SkillForge, rather than a generator-authored bridge from generic multi-turn gain; and (2) a third independent self-evolution mechanism supplies at least 8 source-native aligned units across at least 3 mutation/operation types plus a matched structural test separating targeted entity-grounded or multi-turn intervention evidence from merely more single-turn/non-entity-grounded data. Synthetic proxies, relabeling unrelated entity/schema/tool units, or candidate-mechanism injection do not reopen this HOLD.
